data.name: Selinda
data.gender_notes: Selinda is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Selene was the goddess of the moon. She was often depicted riding a chariot pulled by horses or driving a silver or golden carriage. Selinda may invoke images of lunar cycles, nighttime, and divine protection. The name Selinda carries the meaning “Moon Goddess” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Selinda usually hope their child will grow to embody moon goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of renewal and transformation, as the moon waxes and wanes.
data.etymology: Selinda belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon Goddess.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Selinda total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Selinda, rooted in Greek mythology, may evoke a sense of mystery and enchantment, as it brings to mind the ethereal and captivating figure of Selene, the goddess of the moon. This name may resonate with those who are deeply connected to the night sky, astrology, or the cyclical nature of time. Moreover, Selinda's connection to Selene also implies a sense of grace, beauty, and ever-changing phases.
data.spiritual_significance: Selinda's Greek origin, rooted in the mythology of the goddess Selene, draws a powerful spiritual connection to the cycles of the moon and the transformative energies it represents. This name may evoke a sense of deep introspection and self-reflection, as one contemplates the cycles of birth, death, and rebirth. Additionally, the name Selinda may symbolize a spiritual commitment to embracing change with grace and resilience, much like the moon's cyclical phases. It may serve as a reminder that even in the darkest of times, there is always the promise of a new beginning.
